run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-15T05:58:08Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend is explained by a controller-driven rollout at 2026-11-15T05:56:34Z that replaced the only replica of the ad and payment services. Both replacement containers were pinned at their low CPU limits and CFS-throttled 86-99% of periods while starting, so they did not accept connections for minutes (payment until about 06:00Z, ad until about 05:06Z... correction: ad until about 06:05Z). During that gap every frontend call to grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and, via checkout, oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge was refused at the Service ClusterIPs (ad 100.65.180.246:8080, payment 100.70.188.60:8080), so frontend returned HTTP 500 on /api/data and /api/checkout and the ingress recorded the same 5xx. Affected, each with its own failure evidence: frontend (1734.5 error spans in the window; /api/data and /api/checkout 500s), checkout (69.67 error spans: PlaceOrder server spans plus PaymentService/Charge client spans carrying the charge failure), frontend-proxy (ingress 454.21 and router frontend egress 429.82 error spans). Dependencies observed not serving: ad (no GetAds server spans about 05:58-06:05Z) and payment (no charge spans about 05:58-06:00Z); neither shows application error spans of its own, the failures were connection-level refusals. Checked and healthy or unrelated: cart (its only ERROR series 0; frontend CartService/AddItem and GetCart error series 0), ad and payment application internals (ad ERROR only on flagd EventStream 1.02; payment GET, dns.lookup and tcp.connect ERROR 0), and all 21 otel-demo pods Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and no lastState.terminated, so no crash, OOM or eviction was observed. Contribution toward the error stopped in-window: no new GetAds errors after 06:05Z and no new PlaceOrder errors after 06:00Z. Whether the alert is still firing cannot be verified because no alerting rules are visible in this Prometheus.

claims.text: Frontend error-span volume in the queried window: increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[4560s]) = 1734.53 spans versus 97193.76 for STATUS_CODE_UNSET; the 5-minute error-span rate at 06:00:00Z was 2.7956 spans/s versus 43.042 spans/s Unset, matching an error-rate condition on frontend around alert start 05:58:08Z (the payload's reported value 2.5778 is untrusted input).

Frontend's error spans concentrate on two dependency calls and the routes using them: span_name GET /api/data 387.15, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 387.15, POST /api/checkout 42.68, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 42.68, tcp.connect 15.24, with executing api route (pages) /api/data, GET, POST and executing api route (pages) /api/checkout mirroring those counts, while GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem are 0.

Trace error text identifies connection refusals, not application errors: frontend spans carry otel.status_code=ERROR, http.status_code=500 and rpc.grpc.status_code=14 for AdService/GetAds with exception message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080', and rpc.grpc.status_code=13 for CheckoutService/PlaceOrder with '13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card: could not charge the card: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused"'.

The refused addresses are the Service ClusterIPs, not pod IPs: Service ad has clusterIP 100.65.180.246 port 8080 with selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad, Service payment has clusterIP 100.70.188.60 port 8080 with selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment, both type ClusterIP; a refusal at a ClusterIP means the Service had no serving endpoint.

The endpoints are wired correctly now: Endpoints ad contains exactly one address 100.96.4.142 pointing at pod ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 and Endpoints payment one address 100.96.4.221 pointing at pod payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84, both on port 8080, and the Service selectors match the pods' labels.

Kubernetes rollout events for ad and payment on 2026-11-15: ad-6cb57f76d scaled 0->1 at 05:56:34 with pod ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 Scheduled 05:56:34 and container Started 05:56:36, then old pod ad-554b849958-mbnxm Killed 05:56:37 and ad-554b849958 scaled 1->0 at 05:56:37; payment-9c8ffb665 pod payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 container Started 05:56:37, and old pod payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb Killed 05:56:38 with its ReplicaSet scaled 1->0 at 05:56:38.

Only ad and payment, besides flagd, are at deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 2 in otel-demo: ad owns ReplicaSets ad-554b849958 (created 05:22:50, replicas 0) and ad-6cb57f76d (created 05:56:34, ready 1), payment owns payment-55766d76b9 (created 05:22:49, replicas 0) and payment-9c8ffb665 (created 05:56:34, ready 1), and both old and new ReplicaSets carry the same image tags ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment.

The old and new pod templates for ad and payment are identical in the inspected fields: same env names and values (AD_PORT=8080 and PAYMENT_PORT=8080, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_TEMPORALITY_PREFERENCE=cumulative), same containerPort 8080, no command or args, and same resources (ad requests 10m CPU/225Mi, limits 50m CPU/450Mi; payment requests 10m/80Mi, limits 20m/160Mi).

Neither the old nor the new ad and payment containers define any probe: readiness, liveness and startup probes are absent for httpGet, tcpSocket, grpc and exec (all <none>) in ReplicaSets ad-554b849958, ad-6cb57f76d, payment-55766d76b9 and payment-9c8ffb665; with no readiness probe a pod becomes Ready as soon as its container starts.

The ad service served nothing from about 05:58Z to 06:05Z: its pre-rollout instance series (exported_instance c70d5537...) held at 1415 GetAds server spans from 05:58:00Z onward, while the replacement instance series (exported_instance d90a4539...) first appears at 06:06:00Z with 57 spans; meanwhile frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds STATUS_CODE_ERROR counter rose 421 at 05:57:00Z to 802 at 06:05:00Z and then stayed flat to 06:12:00Z, while its STATUS_CODE_UNSET counter stayed flat at 1415 from 05:58:00Z to 06:04:00Z.

The payment service served nothing from about 05:58Z to 06:00Z: the pre-rollout pod's 'charge' span counter (exported_instance a06abdc3...) stopped rising at 1138 after 05:58:00Z, while the replacement pod's series (exported_instance 72215d3d...) begins at 06:00:00Z with 42 and climbs to 326 by 06:08:00Z; frontend's grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder STATUS_CODE_ERROR counter went 61 at 05:57:00Z, then 70, 101 and 103 at 06:00:00Z, and stayed flat afterward.

The replacement pods were CPU-starved at their limits while starting: pod ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 consumed about 0.047-0.049 cores (limit 0.05) from 05:58Z to 06:05Z and was CFS-throttled in 0.86-0.94 of periods from 05:57Z to 06:04Z, falling to about 0.25-0.43 after 06:05Z, whereas the pre-rollout ad pod sat at 0.002-0.006 cores with 0.006-0.18 throttling; pod payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 was throttled 0.93-0.99 of periods at 05:57-05:59Z at about 0.020 cores (limit 0.02), whereas the pre-rollout payment pod ran at 0.005-0.008 cores with 0.07-0.22 throttling.

checkout recorded its own error spans in the window: 69.67 ERROR spans total, made up of span_name oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 34.83 and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge 34.83, the client span that carries the 'failed to charge card ... connection refused' message.
frontend-proxy recorded error spans mirroring the frontend 5xx at the edge: increase over the window of span_name 'ingress' = 454.21 and 'router frontend egress' = 429.82, both STATUS_CODE_ERROR.

All 21 otel-demo pods are Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and no lastState.terminated reason or exit code, including ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 started 05:56:36Z, payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 started 05:56:37Z and frontend-675fd7b5c5-h8sk5 started 05:22:52Z; the current ad image digest is ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo@sha256:c9d4f943... and payment ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo@sha256:342c8ce5....

Primary cause: the 05:56:34Z rolling update replaced the only replica of ad and payment; because those containers have no readiness or startup probe, Kubernetes retired the old pods about one to two seconds after the new containers started, and because the new containers were pinned at their low CPU limits with 86-99% CFS throttling during startup they did not accept connections for minutes (payment until about 06:00Z, ad until about 06:05Z). Requests then hit the ad and payment ClusterIPs with no serving endpoint and were refused, producing frontend 500s on /api/data and /api/checkout and the RequestErrorRate alert.

Contributing cause: the rollout left zero serving overlap in practice, since with a single replica and readiness equal to 'container started' the controller started the new pod and killed the old one in the same second (Started 05:56:36 and 05:56:37, Killing 05:56:37 and 05:56:38), so there was no backend to serve during cold start.

An unresolved sub-question inside that chain: how much of ad's roughly seven to eight minutes before serving was spent in throttled application initialization versus other startup work is not determined by the available data; the throttling readings show the containers were CPU-bound, but no startup timing or profiling data exists here.

The frontend failure was connection-level and was not caused by errors inside ad or payment: ad's only ERROR series in the window are flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream 1.02 and ResolveBoolean 0, and payment's own ERROR series (GET, dns.lookup, tcp.connect) are 0, so the failed calls never reached those applications.

The failure was transient: no new frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds errors appear after 06:05:00Z (counter flat at 802 through 06:12:00Z) and no new grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder errors after 06:00:00Z (flat at 103), and the replacement ad instance's server-span series then grows 57 at 06:06Z to 129 and 175 while the replacement payment pod's charge spans grow from 42 to 326 by 06:08Z, which contradicts an ongoing configuration fault.

Rejected: pod crash, OOMKilled or eviction of the replacement pods. All otel-demo pods are Running and Ready, restartCount is 0 for every container, no container has a lastState.terminated reason or exit code, and the events seen for the rollout objects are only Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started, SuccessfulCreate, ScalingReplicaSet, Killing and SuccessfulDelete.

Rejected: Service or endpoint misconfiguration such as a wrong selector or port. The Service selectors opentelemetry.io/name=ad and opentelemetry.io/name=payment match the pod labels, Service port 8080 matches containerPort 8080, and both Endpoints objects currently resolve to the running pods, so no mismatch is visible in the objects inspected.

Rejected: flagd feature-flag streaming errors as the cause. Those ERROR spans are on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (ad 1.02, recommendation 4.06, fraud-detection 3.05) and on ResolveBoolean and ResolveInt (0), which are different services and operations from the frontend 500s, and the flagd deployment (revision 2, pod started 05:24:34Z) predates the error onset at 05:57-05:58Z by more than 30 minutes.

Rejected: a fault inside frontend itself. Frontend's ERROR spans are its client spans to AdService/GetAds and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder plus the /api/data and /api/checkout route spans that failed because of them, its pod has restartCount 0, and its CartService client spans recorded 0 errors, so the errors originate in connection attempts to ad and payment rather than in frontend-internal failures.

Add a serving-readiness probe (tcpSocket or gRPC health on 8080) and a startup probe to the ad and payment containers so a rollout does not retire the old replica before the new application accepts connections, and set the rolling update to maxUnavailable 0 with surge capacity.

Raise the CPU limits (ad limit 50m, payment limit 20m) or grant a startup CPU allowance, since both replacement containers were pinned at their limits and throttled 86-99% of periods during cold start, and run more than one replica of ad and payment so a single rollout cannot remove all serving capacity.

Identify and review the change that produced deployment revision 2 for ad and payment (the compared template fields are identical, so the trigger is outside this evidence) and watch the next rollout of these services for the same multi-minute time-to-serve.

gaps: The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so the manifest or config change that produced deployment revision 2 for ad and payment cannot be identified; the compared fields (image tag, env, ports, resources, probes) are identical between the old and new ReplicaSets.

kube_pod_container_info returned no data for the ad and payment pods, so the pre-rollout pods' image digests cannot be compared with the current ones (ad sha256:c9d4f943..., payment sha256:342c8ce5...); whether an image digest changed is unknown.

The events query filtered to Unhealthy|Failed|Evicted|OOM|BackOff|Error returned status no_data, so the absence of such events in otel-demo is not established; only the 18 rollout events for ad and payment were returned by the name-filtered query.

Jaeger retained no traces after 05:57:43Z in the windows queried (traces_search for 06:04-06:06Z and for 06:10:00-06:10:40Z both returned no traces), so error details after 05:57:43Z are unknown and the error-detail sample covers only about 3.4 seconds.
The frontend pod log query returned zero bytes for 05:50-06:10Z (status no_data), so frontend's application-level log errors could not be read.

No alerting rules are visible in this Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and with type=alert both returned no_data, so the alert expression, its evaluation window and whether it is still firing at 06:14:28Z cannot be verified.

The ad container log query for 05:56-06:00Z returned no_data, and its retained stream is only 276 lines whose newest 60 span 06:05:30-06:06:00Z, so what the ad application logged between 05:56:36Z and about 06:03Z is unknown, as is how exactly the minutes before serving were spent.
Container CPU series exist only for pods that still exist and end at 06:08Z, so container resource metrics for ad and payment are unknown after that point in the window.
next_steps: Pull the deployment audit or change record for otel-demo ad and payment revision 2 from the change-history source, which is not integrated in this Run, to identify what was rolled out at 05:56:34Z.

Add readiness and startup probes plus higher startup CPU for ad and payment, scale them beyond one replica, then confirm on the next rollout that time-to-first-served-request stays within the probe budget.

Confirm with the alerting backend whether RequestErrorRate for otel-demo/frontend is still firing, since the rule is not visible in this Prometheus; the underlying ad and payment refusals had stopped by 06:05Z.
